about: Hand-written help topics: how MathLive works inside Obsidian, and the questions people starting with LaTeX ask most. Each one answers in a sentence and links to the exact section of the MathLive docs, or runs the plugin feature it is about. 'basic' topics are the getting-started list shown before anything is typed. scripts/build-help-index.mjs makes the rest of the index from the docs themselves.

entries.title: Start a formula
entries.answer: Type $…$ for a formula inside a sentence, or $$…$$ on its own line, and click it to edit. Or run “Add inline math” or “Add full-line math” from the command palette.
entries.keywords: new add create insert write math equation formula inline block display dollar sign start begin how use

entries.title: Write a fraction
entries.answer: Type / and the part before it becomes the numerator. Type the denominator, then → to leave it.
entries.keywords: fraction divide division over numerator denominator ratio slash frac half

entries.title: Write a power or superscript
entries.answer: Type ^ then the exponent, like x^2. Press → or Space to come back down.
entries.keywords: power exponent superscript squared cubed raise to the power upper index ^ e to the x exponential e^x

entries.title: Write a subscript or index
entries.answer: Type _ then the index, like x_1. Press → or Space to come back up.
entries.keywords: subscript index lower underscore indices x sub n

entries.title: Write a square root
entries.answer: Type sqrt, or press Alt+V (⌥V on a Mac). For an nth root press Alt+Shift+V.
entries.keywords: square root radical sqrt root cube nth

entries.title: Type Greek letters
entries.answer: Type the letter's name: alpha, beta, theta, pi, Sigma. Capitalize it for the capital letter.
entries.keywords: greek letter alpha beta gamma delta theta lambda mu pi sigma omega symbol

entries.title: Move around a formula
entries.answer: Use the arrow keys to move in and out of fractions, powers and roots. Tab jumps to the next empty box, and Space leaves the part you are in.
entries.keywords: move navigate cursor arrow keys tab next placeholder empty box get out exit leave escape go back jump

entries.title: Type symbols with shortcuts
entries.answer: Many symbols come from what you would write in plain text: >= gives ≥, != gives ≠, -> gives →, oo gives ∞, xx gives ×, +- gives ±. Ctrl+Z undoes one you didn't want.
entries.keywords: inline shortcuts symbols ascii type special characters operators arrows not equal less greater infinity times plus minus

entries.title: Type LaTeX commands directly
entries.answer: Type \ and a command name, like \vec or \mathbb, then Enter. MathLive suggests commands as you type. Your note always keeps plain LaTeX.
entries.keywords: latex mode command backslash raw code tex suggestions type latex directly enter latex

entries.title: Use the math keyboard
entries.answer: Click the keyboard icon on a full-line formula or in the editor window. Switch layouts for numbers, symbols, letters and Greek, press Shift for more, and long-press a key for related symbols.
entries.keywords: virtual keyboard on screen math keyboard buttons tablet phone touch layouts greek symbols numbers

entries.title: Find a command in the ☰ menu
entries.answer: Click ☰ on a formula, or right-click inside it, for matrices, colors, text, font styles and more. Alt+Space opens it from the keyboard.
entries.keywords: menu context menu right click hamburger options insert matrix color style variant

entries.title: Make a matrix
entries.answer: Pick Insert Matrix in the ☰ menu (or right-click in the formula) and choose its size. From the keyboard: type ( or [, the first entry, then Alt+Tab for a new column and Alt+Enter for a new row (⌥Tab and ⌥Return on a Mac).
entries.keywords: matrix matrices table array grid rows columns vector determinant pmatrix bmatrix

entries.title: Add or remove matrix rows and columns
entries.answer: Right-click a cell of the matrix and choose to add or remove a row or column next to it.
entries.keywords: add row column remove delete resize shape

entries.title: Write several lines or align equations
entries.answer: In a full-line formula, press Enter for a new line. MathLive keeps the lines in one aligned block.
entries.keywords: new line multiple lines align equations system break line several rows aligned gather

entries.title: Write a piecewise function
entries.answer: Use the cases environment: type \begin{cases} in LaTeX mode, or start with { and add rows with Alt+Enter.
entries.keywords: piecewise cases brace conditions function defined by parts if otherwise

entries.title: Write words inside a formula
entries.answer: Type " (Shift+') to switch to text, and again to switch back. Spaces work as normal in text.
entries.keywords: text words space spaces sentence plain text mode label units \text write words

entries.title: Write an integral, sum or limit
entries.answer: Type int, sum or lim. Fill in the bounds with the boxes, and Tab moves to the next one.
entries.keywords: integral sum summation sigma limit lim product bounds calculus integrate series

entries.title: Write a derivative
entries.answer: Write d/dx as a fraction: d, /, then dx. Type del for ∂ in partial derivatives, and dx after an integral comes out upright on its own.
entries.keywords: derivative differentiate partial d/dx dy dx prime calculus del nabla gradient

entries.title: Write a vector arrow or hat
entries.answer: Type \vec, \hat, \bar or \overline in LaTeX mode, then the letter.
entries.keywords: vector arrow hat bar overline accent dot tilde above letter mean average unit vector

entries.title: Write ℝ, ℕ and other number sets
entries.answer: Type RR for ℝ, NN for ℕ, ZZ for ℤ, QQ for ℚ and CC for ℂ. Type in for ∈.
entries.keywords: real numbers natural integers rational complex blackboard bold set element of in mathbb

entries.title: Write brackets that grow
entries.answer: Type ( [ { or | and the closing one appears and grows with what is inside.
entries.keywords: brackets parentheses braces absolute value delimiters big left right grow fence abs

entries.title: Color part of a formula
entries.answer: Select it, then pick a color in the ☰ menu. In LaTeX it is \textcolor{red}{…}.
entries.keywords: color colour highlight red blue background textcolor

entries.title: Make letters bold, upright or script
entries.answer: Select them and pick a style in the ☰ menu, or use \mathbf, \mathrm, \mathcal in LaTeX mode.
entries.keywords: bold upright roman italic font style calligraphic script fraktur mathbf mathrm mathcal

entries.title: Write chemistry formulas
entries.answer: Use \ce in LaTeX mode: \ce{H2O} or \ce{2H2 + O2 -> 2H2O}.
entries.keywords: chemistry chemical equation reaction molecule mhchem ce h2o

entries.title: Undo a change
entries.answer: Ctrl+Z (⌘Z on a Mac) undoes the last change in the formula, Ctrl+Y redoes it. Ctrl+Z also turns a shortcut back into the letters you typed.
entries.keywords: undo redo mistake revert go back ctrl z wrong symbol

entries.title: Select part of a formula
entries.answer: Hold Shift and use the arrow keys, or drag with the mouse. Ctrl+A selects the whole formula.
entries.keywords: select selection highlight mark part copy shift arrows

entries.title: Leave the formula
entries.answer: Click outside it, or press → at its end (← at its start) to go back to your text.
entries.keywords: leave exit get out of formula back to text done finish stop editing escape

entries.title: See the LaTeX behind a formula
entries.answer: Run “Show raw LaTeX in notes, or editors again” from the command palette or the ⋮ menu of a note. Run it again to get the editors back.
entries.keywords: raw latex source code see latex show latex source mode edit latex text plain

entries.title: Edit a long formula in a bigger window
entries.answer: Click ⤢ next to the formula. The editor window has the math keyboard and the ✨ tools, and Ctrl+Enter puts the formula back.
entries.keywords: bigger window expand modal editor window long formula full screen popup larger

entries.title: Find a well-known formula
entries.answer: Search thousands of formulas by name, by what they do, in your language, or by a bit of LaTeX, and put one in your note. Free.
entries.keywords: find formula library search known formula equation law theorem physics chemistry statistics quadratic pythagoras look up

entries.title: Scan a formula instead of typing it
entries.answer: Click ✨ next to a formula and scan a screenshot, an area of your screen, or a photo. The LaTeX lands in your formula, ready to edit.
entries.keywords: scan image screenshot photo picture ocr convert picture to latex copy formula from pdf website video handwriting camera

entries.title: Draw a formula by hand
entries.answer: Write it with your mouse or pen, or scan the QR code and draw it on your phone. You see the formula as you draw.
entries.keywords: draw handwriting handwrite pen stylus tablet mouse sketch write by hand phone qr

entries.title: Change a formula by describing it
entries.answer: Pick Magic edit in the ✨ menu next to a formula and type or say what to change, like “square the denominator”. Undo puts it back.
entries.keywords: magic edit ai change rewrite describe voice speak modify transform simplify

entries.title: Turn a PDF into notes
entries.answer: Open a PDF and click “Convert to notes” at its top right. Every formula becomes editable LaTeX in a Markdown note.
entries.keywords: pdf convert notes lecture slides paper document import markdown

entries.title: Use Quick Latex style shorthands
entries.answer: Turn on Quick Latex shorthands in Settings → MathLive: type al and Space for α, sq and Space for a root. You can add your own or import Quick Latex's.
entries.keywords: shorthands quick latex snippets abbreviations custom shortcuts own shortcuts al space latex suite import

entries.title: Show formulas the normal Obsidian way
entries.answer: In Settings → MathLive turn on “Edit only the formula at the cursor”, or turn off the inline or block widgets.
entries.keywords: turn off disable widgets normal rendering obsidian mathjax only at cursor stop editor preview

entries.title: Add a formula with a hotkey
entries.answer: Open Settings → Hotkeys, search MathLive, and give “Add inline math” or “Add full-line math” a key.
entries.keywords: hotkey shortcut keyboard shortcut bind key command palette add formula quickly

entries.title: See every keyboard shortcut
entries.answer: The MathLive docs list every key combination and every typed shortcut.
entries.keywords: all keyboard shortcuts keybindings list reference cheat sheet keys

entries.title: See every LaTeX command MathLive knows
entries.answer: MathLive supports over 800 LaTeX commands, listed by topic with what each looks like.
entries.keywords: all latex commands list reference symbols supported cheat sheet

entries.title: Everything MathLive can do in Obsidian
entries.answer: Scanning, drawing, the formula library, Magic edit and PDF to notes, each with a button to try it.
entries.keywords: features guide what can it do overview tour help plugin
